Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Supervisory Psychologist: Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) with a major or equivalent in psychology. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes 1) providing consultative services in the designing, planning, and/or implementation of protocols within an organization's performance enhancement program; 2) devising strategies and/or interventions to help facilitate peak human performance; 3) developing and/or conducting performance psychology or mental skills training to maximize physical aptitude such as confidence, attention control, energy management, imagery, and goal setting; 4) instructing students at a higher level academic institution; and, 5) leading personnel and/or projects. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas:
Administration and ManagementLeadershipPsychology

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The U.S. Military Academy, West Point, NY is an academic institution located in the Hudson River Valley, 50 miles from New York City. The historic site is the oldest continuously occupied military post in America. West Point is a self-contained city with housing, a Department of Public Works, libraries, hospital, fire department, chapels, and restaurants. Employees have access to Eisenhower Hall Theater, Hudson Valley's performing arts center, and recreational facilities.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Dean, Center for Enhanced Performance
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Provide professional mentoring and guidance in the delivery of the Performance Psychology Program to U.S. Military Academy cadets and cadet organizations to ensure quality and programmatic consistency.
Advise Center for Enhanced Performance staff members in all matters pertaining to performance psychology.
Provide guidance in the application of performance psychology theory and practice to military outreach activities; supervise curriculum development; and provide input on future staff decisions.
Coordinate with academic staff and coaches regarding any problems encountered with the cadets.

Provide advice regarding appropriate staff responses toward a cadet and addresses the environmental factors that will produce more self-reliance, reduce anxiety and achieve effective behavior changes.
Formulate and oversee assessment activities for all performance psychology training; and develop curricula in response to advances in the field of sport psychology.
Serve as Course Director and determine curriculum content for various courses including RS 101 (Student Success Course) and RS 104 (Introduction to Performance Psychology).
Coordinate with the Department of Behavioral Sciences and Leadership for the oversight and administration of PL 360 (Psychology of Elite Performance).
Perform the full range of administrative and technical supervisory duties.

MajorDuties: Serves as the subject matter expert on Individual Medical Readiness (IMR).
Collects, inputs, and manages medical readiness information for the Battalion/Squadron and subordinate units.

Assists in processing, documenting, storing, and retrieving medical records information IAW laws and regulations.
Prepares, reviews, schedules, monitors, and submits line of duty investigations and packets for required medical review and/or action.
Performs other duties as assigned.
